Stocks climbed on Thursday even though the PPI was much hotter than expected.Getty Images

Stocks climbed again on Tuesday, with chipmakers leading the session as they recover from a sharp sell-off from the past weeks.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged up 0.03%, while the S&P 500 did so 0.60%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite overperformed, jumping 1.18%. Broadcom, Micron and Advanced Micro Devices were among the names that led the index higher.

Traders will now look at the Federal Reserve's policy decision on Wednesday, when the central bank is expected to leave rates unchanged, offering borrowers a reprieve after September's increase. But with inflation gathering momentum and the economy showing few signs of weakening, another hike could follow before policymakers are ready to declare their work finished.

The expected pause, however, comes ahead of government reports that could strengthen the argument for further tightening. Data scheduled for Thursday are projected to show faster inflation in September and stronger economic growth in the third quarter, supported by consumer spending and business investment tied to artificial intelligence.

Economists expect the annual increase in the personal consumption expenditures price index, the Fed's preferred inflation measure, to reach 3.6%, up from 3.4% in August. Higher gasoline prices linked to the conflicts in the Middle East account for part of that acceleration, but price pressures have also spread to airfares, rents and computers.

That broader increase complicates the Fed's effort to bring inflation back to its 2% target. However, September's unemployment rate stood at 4.2%, while weekly applications for unemployment benefits remained exceptionally low.

The main reason to wait lies in the bond market. After September's rate hike, the yield on the 10-year Treasury climbed toward its highest levels in nearly 25 years, threatening to restrain activity more sharply than officials intended.

Higher Treasury yields can raise financing costs for households and businesses, effectively doing some of the Fed's work. New York Fed President John Williams and Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson subsequently indicated that policymakers could wait for additional evidence before deciding their next move.

But that rationale became less straightforward late last week, when bond yields retreated during a stock selloff driven by concerns about the sustainability of AI demand. An easing in financial conditions could weaken the case for an extended pause.

Many top stocks are down this year, even though the S&P 500 has continued to soar to new heights. That can happen when a good chunk of stocks are up big, including Micron Technology, AMD, and CrowdStrike -- they've all more than doubled in value thus far in 2026.

At the other end of the spectrum, however, are some more troubled stocks. And for long-term investors, this is where the deals can be found: in stocks that aren't doing well of late but still have strong businesses worth investing in. Three magnificent stocks that are trading near their 52-week lows that could be great long-term buys right now include Netflix (NASDAQ:NFLX), American Express (NYSE:AXP), and Uber Technologies (NYSE:UBER).

Missed AI's "Act 1"? Act 2 Could Be 14x Bigger. Most investors think they missed the AI boat because they didn't buy Nvidia in 2005. But according to our analysts, we're only at the end of "Act 1"—the R&D phase. "Act 2" is the global rollout. Continue »

Image source: Getty Images.

Netflix

Shares of streaming company Netflix are down more than 30% this year. Concerns about its slowing growth are weighing on the stock, and with Paramount and HBO content now coming together under Skydance, competition may also intensify in the near future.

However, the business is still growing in double digits, with Netflix forecasting 13% revenue growth for the full year. Paying 18 times earnings for that kind of growth is more than reasonable, especially with the company still pursuing growth opportunities in live sports. Plus, all it takes is one hot new series or movie to get people excited again. Over the years, Netflix has shown it can produce its own content well, proving it can compete with the top studios in Hollywood.

It hit a new 52-week low on Tuesday, and with a light valuation, this could be an excellent stock to buy right now.

American Express

Another stock that hasn't been doing well this year is American Express. Shares of the credit card company have declined by over 15%, and this is even as the business has proven to be fairly robust and resilient amid challenging economic conditions. By targeting more affluent customers, the business is in an excellent position to do well even when other companies struggle.

Last week, the company released its third-quarter numbers, which showed solid 9% growth in its most recent period. Adjusted net income of $3.2 billion was up 11% year over year, as American Express demonstrates that it can continue to deliver solid numbers, even when economic conditions aren't ideal.

Broadcom Drops 6% in a Month: Buy, Sell or Hold the AVGO Stock?

Broadcom AVGO shares have dropped 5.8% over the past month, underperforming the broader Zacks Computer and Technology sector's drop of 5.1%. The company's shares have suffered from margin pressure from the rising AI mix, supply constraints, a concentrated AI clientele and weak non-AI business.

AVGO shares have also underperformed NVIDIA NVDA, Advanced Micro Devices AMD and Skyworks SWKS over the same period. Shares of NVIDIA have dropped 5.6%, while AMD and Skyworks have declined 12.6% and 4.8%, respectively. So, what should investors do with the AVGO stock post the dip? Let us find out.

AVGO Stock's Price Performance
Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

AVGO's Prospects Suffer From Multiple Challenges

Broadcom's rapidly expanding custom accelerator business is weighing on consolidated gross margins because XPUs carry an increasing proportion of expensive memory content. In the third quarter of 2026, non-GAAP gross margin declined 210 basis points sequentially to 75%. AVGO expects gross margin to decline further to approximately 73% in the fourth quarter compared with 78% in the year-ago period. Continued growth in lower-margin AI hardware relative to software could limit profitability expansion, although operating leverage should provide some offset.

AVGO faces limitations involving advanced semiconductor wafers, high-bandwidth memory, substrates and optical components. The company's custom AI accelerator business currently depends on six major customers, exposing AVGO to changes in hyperscaler capital spending and product strategies. Competition from NVIDIA, AMD, MediaTek and customers' internal semiconductor development teams could intensify over time. Any loss of design wins, customer insourcing or moderation in AI infrastructure investments could affect revenue growth and long-term earnings visibility.

Moreover, Broadcom's non-AI semiconductor business continues to experience relatively modest growth compared with its AI portfolio. In the third quarter of 2026, non-AI revenues increased only 5% year over year to $4.2 billion and remained flat sequentially. While broadband and server storage demand improved, weakness in wireless partially offset these gains. Continued softness across traditional semiconductor end markets could constrain revenue diversification. Broader concerns surrounding the sustainability of AI infrastructure spending have also weighed on semiconductor stocks, including Broadcom.

Can AVGO's Strong AI Growth Boost Competitive Prowess?

Broadcom expects AI semiconductor revenues to reach approximately $58 billion in fiscal 2026, followed by $115 billion in fiscal 2027 and $230 billion in fiscal 2028. These projections reflect increasing deployments of custom accelerators and AI networking equipment by leading frontier-model developers.

Broadcom's long-term agreement with Google to develop and supply future generations of TPUs and networking products through 2031 strengthens revenue visibility. Anthropic is expected to deploy an additional 5 gigawatts of TPU capacity in 2027 and 10 incremental gigawatts in 2028. OpenAI is targeting more than 5 gigawatts of custom accelerator deployments in 2028, while Meta is expected to deploy approximately 3 gigawatts through 2028. These customer roadmaps offer substantial multiyear growth opportunities.

Broadcom's expertise in advanced packaging, high-speed SerDes, chip-to-chip interconnects and high-bandwidth memory integration provides a competitive advantage. The company's ability to co-develop accelerators optimized for customers' specific AI workloads could support additional design wins. Increasing semiconductor complexity and the transition toward multi-die architectures may further strengthen demand for Broadcom's engineering capabilities.

Growing enterprise requirements for data sovereignty, cybersecurity and cost-effective AI infrastructure could strengthen adoption of VMware Cloud Foundation and VMware Private AI Cloud. These platforms enable organizations to operate AI workloads alongside existing enterprise applications. Rising subscription adoption and recurring revenues could improve software revenue visibility and support Broadcom's long-term profitability.

However, Broadcom's projected growth relies heavily on sustained capital expenditures by a limited number of hyperscalers and AI model developers. Higher HBM content, increasingly complex packaging and growing dependence on custom accelerators could continue pressuring gross margins. Although Broadcom expects operating leverage to offset some dilution, rising manufacturing costs or unfavorable semiconductor pricing could constrain long-term margin expansion. The company is facing stiff competition, which is a concern for investors.
